title: Age-predicted maximal heart rate revisited
publisher: Journal of the American College of Cardiology
claims: A meta-analysis collected group mean maximal heart rate values from 351 studies involving 492 groups and 18,712 subjects.
Maximal heart rate was strongly related to age (r = -0.90), with the regression equation 208 - 0.7 × age.
A laboratory-based cross-validation in 514 healthy subjects produced 209 - 0.7 × age, virtually identical to the meta-analysis equation.
The regression line was not different between men and women and was not influenced by wide variations in habitual physical activity.
The authors suggest that the 220 - age equation significantly underestimates maximal heart rate in older adults.
The authors recommend 208 - 0.7 × age as a regression equation to predict maximal heart rate in healthy adults.

claimVerification.note: 原文：“a meta-analytic approach was used to collect group mean HRmax values from 351 studies involving 492 groups and 18,712 subjects.”
原文：“HRmax was strongly related to age (r = −0.90), using the equation of 208 − 0.7 × age.” Results 亦述男女均 r = −0.90。
原文：“HRmax was measured in 514 healthy subjects… The regression equation obtained in the laboratory-based study (209 − 0.7 × age) was virtually identical to that obtained from the meta-analysis.”

原文：“The regression line was not different between men and women, nor was it influenced by wide variations in habitual physical activity levels.” Results 给出 sedentary 211−0.8×age、active 207−0.7×age、endurance-trained 206−0.7×age。
原文：“Our findings suggest that the prevailing equation significantly underestimates HRmax in older adults.” 保留 suggest 与 significantly。

原文结论：“1) A regression equation to predict HRmax is 208 − 0.7 × age in healthy adults.” 讨论并称该式“significantly different from the traditional 220 − age equation”。原文未用“recommend”一词，但整篇主旨即为以该式替代 220−age，claim 属同义转述。
